model: Bank FCFE at cost of equity (engine route), net debt zero, CET1 retention on risk-weighted-asset growth, AT1 and preference distributions charged in the flow

inputs.base_revenue_definition: FY2026E operating income (net interest income + net fee and commission income + other net non-interest income, after the Bank's own 'operating income' definition), RMB millions. FY2026 (Dec year-end) is unreported: H1 2026 actual RMB426.3bn (+10.48% YoY, Analysis.json / interim announcement) + H2 2026E ~RMB369bn (H2 2025 actual 354,966 x ~1.04: the H1 surge was front-loaded by +16% non-interest income on bond-trading gains, NIM stabilised at 1.37%, H2 assumed to grow at the slower NII run-rate). FY2025 actual 740,871 (AR FY2025 line 723; quarterly 185,990 / 199,915 / 174,376 / 180,590 in Q1-Q4 order, so H1 2025 = 385,905). FY2024 728,570; FY2023 745,615; FY2022 758,155; FY2021 764,706. Using FY2026E as FY0 puts year 1 = FY2027, one year from the valuation date as the engine's end-of-year discounting requires.
inputs.share_count_basis: 261,600,381,459 ordinary shares at 2025-12-31 (AR FY2025 share-capital table: 21,183.1m A-shares incl. the 11,589.4m issued to the MOF on 24 June 2025 at RMB9.06, + 240,417.3m H-shares). All A and H shares are ordinary, par RMB1, rank pari passu; no options, convertibles or other dilutive instruments (basic = diluted EPS 1.30). Domestic preference shares convert only on a regulatory trigger event and are carried as other equity instruments. Held FLAT: no SBC, no buybacks (state-controlled bank, ShareRepurchases 0 every year). NOT modelled: a possible second MOF-led recapitalisation round (reported Sept 2026 for ICBC/ABC); the 2025 placement was at a 6% premium to market, so a repeat would be roughly value-neutral to H-share holders at today's 0.63x book but would dilute per-share book and EPS. Count unchanged at 2026-06-30 (no issuance in H1 2026 reported).
inputs.funding_note: Net debt held at ZERO by construction (house bank policy). Deposits from customers RMB30.8tn, borrowings from central banks RMB1.0tn, interbank funding and RMB bonds/TLAC instruments are operating funding whose cost is inside net interest income; cash and balances with central banks RMB1.06tn (CSV cash_and_equivalents) are reserve requirements and liquidity held against that funding, not surplus. The flow capitalised is free cash flow to equity (profit to ordinary shareholders less the CET1 retained to fund RWA growth) at the cost of equity, so nothing is added or deducted for debt or cash. The CSV total_debt column is NULL for this ticker by design.
inputs.fcf_definition: Bank FCFE, not owner FCF. last_fcf = FY2025 ordinary cash dividends declared: RMB3.887 per 10 shares x 261,600m = RMB101,684m (interim 48,605 paid Dec 2025 + final 53,079 paid July 2026), 30.5% of profit to ordinary shareholders (338,906 attributable less 5,420 AT1/preference distributions = 333,486). Forward FCFE = profit to common less the CET1 retention needed to hold the CET1 ratio at ~14.5% while RWA grow; distributions above the 30% policy are capital the model treats as distributable once RWA growth slows (CCB has no buyback mechanism, so in practice this would arrive as a rising payout ratio or as CET1 accumulating above target -- the market's refusal to pay for that accumulation is the main reason the H-share trades at 0.63x book). CSV FreeCashFlow is empty and OperatingCashFlow (RMB2.1tn FY2025, 338bn FY2024) is deposit/trading flow, not cash generation. interest_income = 0: interest is the bank's revenue, not excess-cash income.
inputs.dividends_paid_note: RMB108,178m cash dividends paid in FY2025 (cash flow statement) = ordinary (final FY2024 51,502 + interim FY2025 48,605) + preference 2,142 + perpetual-bond interest 3,278 + subsidiary NCI dividends; the last_fcf figure uses the FY2025-declared ordinary dividends instead.
inputs.sbc_source: SBC-zero: CCB has no share-based payment scheme (state-owned; no equity incentive plan disclosed in the FY2018-FY2025 annual reports, StockBasedComp empty in the CSV). Basic = diluted EPS. House and street bases coincide; band_position is null by construction.
inputs.fx_note: fx_rate converts CNY (model, the Bank reports in RMB) to HKD (H-share quote): CNYHKD=X 1.1721 at 2026-10-10T03:38Z, Yahoo Finance (i.e. USD/CNY ~6.64 against the 7.78 HKD peg). Per-share values are per ordinary share; the H-share and A-share are the same class, so intrinsic_value (HKD) is comparable to current_price and the *_cny twins are RMB per share, comparable to the A-share. Parity check: Shanghai A-share 601939.SS closed RMB10.98 on 2026-10-09 = HKD12.87, vs the H-share HKD9.735 = RMB8.31 -- a 32% A/H premium, in line with the Hang Seng AH Premium Index (~130s) and the structural pattern for the Big Four; it is a market-segmentation gap, not an FX error. FY2025 ordinary DPS RMB0.3887 = HKD0.4556 = 4.7% trailing yield at current_price.
inputs.fy0: FY2026E (year ending 2026-12-31, unreported: H1 2026 actual + H2 estimate)
inputs.balance_sheet_date: 2025-12-31 (FY2025 annual report; H1 2026 interim not extracted into this folder -- only its headline figures from Analysis.json are used: CAR 19.42%, NPL 1.29%, NIM 1.37%, attributable profit RMB169.6bn)
inputs.wacc_rationale: Single CNY cost of equity 9.5% across all scenarios (risk charged once, via the scenario weights). Built in the flows' own currency: 10-year China Government Bond ~1.8% (ASSUMPTION, not fetched; the PBOC easing cycle has the 10Y CGB in the 1.6-2.0% range since 2025) + beta ~1.05 to CSI 300 x China ERP ~6.5% = ~8.6%, plus ~0.9pt for the risks a Chinese ERP does not price for an H-share holder: state-directed lending (the 'Five Priorities' mandate allocates credit for policy, not return), governance (majority MOF/Huijin control, no buyback lever, payout set by the state), and capital-account/RMB translation risk for the HKD holder. House precedents: MFG 9.0% JPY, WF 10.0% KRW, HSBC 10.5% USD (incl. HK/China premium). A USD or HKD rate (UST 10Y ~5.3%, 10Y HK gov ~4%) would overcharge RMB flows by the rate differential; HKD translation risk is carried by fx_rate and the bear weight, not the discount rate. At 9.5% and a 3% terminal growth the base case's ~9.5% steady-state ROE on common, reached only after a decade in which 30-40% payouts fund policy-pace RWA growth, values the bank at ~0.87x current book (RMB11.49), between the H-share (0.63x) and A-share (0.83x) prices and a little above the latter.
inputs.lease_treatment: Bank: IFRS 16 right-of-use depreciation (inside D&A RMB29.3bn) and interest on lease liabilities (RMB22.0bn liabilities, AR FY2025 line 14854) sit inside operating expenses, i.e. inside pre-tax profit. lease_cost_pct_path = 0, no lease liability in the bridge.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, inside the flow: the margin is calibrated to net profit attributable to equity shareholders of the Bank (338,906 FY2025, after NCI of 884) LESS distributions on other equity instruments (FY2025: domestic preference dividend 2,142 + perpetual-bond interest 987 + 1,280 + 1,011 = 5,420; FY2026E ~6,300 after the RMB40bn undated AT1 bonds issued May 2025 start paying), which are charged to retained earnings, not to profit. Other equity instruments of RMB199,977m (preference 59,977 + perpetual bonds 140,000) are therefore stripped from equity for the book-value cross-checks. Neither NCI nor the AT1 instruments is deducted again in the bridge.
inputs.engine_mapping: revenue = operating income (see base_revenue_definition); 'ebitda margin' = pre-tax profit to ordinary shareholders (after credit impairment RMB133.3bn, operating expenses incl. the 29.4% cost-to-income, taxes and surcharges, NCI and the AT1/preference distributions grossed up at the tax rate) as % of operating income -- FY2025 actual 50.2% (333,486 / (1 - 0.107) / 740,871); FY2026E ~49.0% (H1 2026 attributable +4.6% on operating income +10.5% => impairment and opex absorbing the revenue beat; 353.5bn attributable - 6.3bn AT1 = 347.2bn to common, / 0.89 / 795,000); da_pct 0 (depreciation and amortisation RMB29.3bn is inside operating expenses, IT/branch capex RMB23.6bn is maintenance funded within them); cash tax = the Bank's effective income-tax rate (10.7% FY2025, 12.5% FY2024, 14.6% FY2023; well below the 25% statutory rate because RMB65.8bn of PRC government and local-government bond interest is non-taxable, AR FY2025 note 12207-12214; cash tax paid 62,767 = 16.5% of PBT in FY2025 on provision timing differences) -- modelled at 12% rising to 14% as the bond exemption's share of a growing profit base erodes; 'capex' = CET1 retention; wc 0; 'wacc' = CNY cost of equity. Implied multiples at the weighted value are checked by hand in RMB per share against net assets per ordinary share RMB13.24 (3,663,411 - 199,977 = 3,463,434 / 261,600m, AR FY2025 line 756) and EPS 1.30.
inputs.capital_anchor: CET1 capital RMB3,464,852m / RWA RMB23,685,171m = 14.63% at 2025-12-31 (AR FY2025 line 748-751; 14.48% end-2024, 13.15% end-2023 before the 2024 capital-rules change and the RMB105bn MOF placement). Total capital ratio 19.69%, 19.42% at H1 2026 (Analysis.json) -- RWA grew faster than capital in H1 2026 (+12.5% asset growth FY2025, +8.4% RWA). Regulatory minimum for CCB as a bucket-2 G-SIB ~9.0% CET1 (5% + 2.5% conservation + 1.5% G-SIB), so ~5.5pts of headroom. Projected end-2026E: RWA ~RMB25.34tn (+7%), CET1 ~RMB3.70tn (end-2025 + 347bn profit to common - ~103bn ordinary dividends paid in 2026 - regulatory deductions) = ~14.6%. Retention = 14.5% x that year's RWA growth in every scenario (held at the Bank's own operating level rather than the regulatory floor: management has never run the ratio down, and the state's TLAC and 'Five Priorities' lending agenda argues for keeping the buffer); terminal-year retention = CET1 x g so the ratio is constant in perpetuity.
inputs.data_quality_warning: Metrics CSV: Revenue = operating income (fine); FreeCashFlow empty and OperatingCashFlow is deposit/trading flow (do not use); ShareholdersEquity excludes NCI but INCLUDES RMB200bn of preference shares and perpetual bonds (strip them for common equity; the CSV's FY2025 equity 3,663,411 vs common 3,463,434); SharesOutstanding FY2025 = 256,107m is the WEIGHTED average (the MOF shares were issued 24 June 2025), year-end issued count is 261,600m; EPS in RMB per share. H1 2026 interim was not extracted into this folder as of this build -- its headline figures come from Analysis.json (interim announcement Aug 2026) and should be confirmed when the interim is added. sanity_check.py applies inputs.fx_rate in the wrong direction (known systemic bug, see memory): any P/E or P/B it prints will be off by ~1.37x (1.1721 squared) unless it bridges HKD->CNY correctly; hand-computed multiples are in sanity_check_note.
inputs.notes: MODEL: bank -> dcf-methods routing row 'Bank, non-bank deposit taker, thrift'. Run as FCFE at cost of equity through the component engine, the house precedent for banks (HSBC, LYG, WF, MFG, HDB, IBN, BMO, USB, WFC, NAB.AX). First valuation of this ticker, no MEMORY.md entry. Not an owner-FCF DCF: deposits are operating funding, OCF is meaningless, net debt is zero by construction and no debt or cash is bridged. Qualitative context from 0939.HK_Analysis.json (2026-10-12): NIM 1.34% FY2025 -> 1.37% H1 2026 (first uptick after four years of compression), NPL 1.31% -> 1.29%, real-estate development NPL 4.93%, mortgages ~22% of loans, cost-to-income 29.44%, credit impairment +10.5% to RMB133.3bn, ~30% payout policy since 2015, RMB105bn MOF recapitalisation June 2025, H1 2026 operating income +10.5% / attributable profit +4.6%. Risks: China property and LGFV credit cycle, policy-directed lending at sub-economic returns, further PBOC easing on a 1.3% NIM, state control of payout. The valuation is in RMB first; the HKD figure moves one-for-one with CNY/HKD.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: terminal nominal growth for a mature Chinese megabank (China nominal GDP ~4-5% less NIM drift), bracketed by revenue 5yr CAGR 0.7% and EPS 5yr CAGR 4.2%
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr/5yr CAGR 8.6%/9.1% vs revenue -0.8%/+0.7% and EPS 0.5%/4.2% (>30% apart): equity growth is retained earnings at a 30% payout plus RMB105bn of MOF capital and RMB40bn net AT1 issuance, while revenue has been flat for five years under NIM compression (2.19% -> 1.34%). Equity CAGR is therefore not a forward growth measure; common BVPS grew 6.8%/yr over three years and is the better compounding proxy, and the projection is driven from operating income with a 3% terminal.
historical_growth.notes: CAGRs to FY2025 from 0939.HK_Metrics.csv (operating income, EPS RMB per share, equity attributable incl. AT1 instruments) and the AR FY2025 five-year table (net assets per ordinary share 13.24 vs 10.86 FY2022). FCF CAGRs not meaningful for a bank (OCF swung from 338bn to 2.1tn between FY2024 and FY2025 on deposit flows).

base.growth_rationale: FY2027 +4%: NIM holds ~1.35-1.40% as the deposit-repricing lag finally offsets the 2024-25 LPR cuts (H1 2026 NIM 1.37% vs 1.34% FY2025), interest-earning assets grow ~7% (loans +7.5% FY2025), fee income +5-6% on wealth management, custody and bancassurance, other non-interest income normalises from the H1 2026 bond-gain surge. Fades to 3% = terminal (China nominal GDP ~4-5% less continued margin drift as the loan book is steered to inclusive/green/tech lending at policy pricing).
base.margin_rationale: Pre-tax profit to ordinary shareholders / operating income. FY2025 actual 50.2%, FY2026E ~49.0%. Credit impairment held ~18-19% of operating income (FY2025 18.0%, i.e. ~50bps of gross loans; real-estate development NPL 4.93% and special-mention 1.77% argue against assuming it falls), cost-to-income drifting from 29.4% toward 30% as IT/AI spend and wage growth outrun flat revenue, AT1 distributions ~0.8%. Steady-state ROE on common equity ~9.5-10% in FY2027 settling to ~9.5%, against the 9.5% CoE -- i.e. about 1.0x book at steady state.
base.capex_rationale: Equity retention, not capex: 14.5% x RWA growth for the year (6.5%, 6.0%, 5.5%, 5.0%, 4.5%, 4.0%, 3.5%, then 3.0% = terminal growth) from an opening RWA of RMB25.34tn (end-2026E), expressed as % of that year's operating income. RWA grow faster than revenue in the early years because the balance sheet keeps expanding at policy pace (+8.4% FY2025) while NIM drifts; the two converge at 3% by FY2034. Resulting payout: ~32% of profit to common in FY2027 (RMB114bn vs the 30% policy -- the current dividend is roughly what holding 14.5% CET1 at 6.5% RWA growth allows), rising to ~63% by FY2036 as RWA growth slows; the increment above 30% is the capital that would otherwise accumulate above target.
base.tax_rationale: Effective income-tax rate 10.7% FY2025 / 12.5% FY2024 / 14.6% FY2023 on non-taxable government-bond interest (RMB65.8bn FY2025); rises as profit grows against a bond portfolio that grows more slowly. 25% statutory is never reached. Cash tax paid ran 16.5-22% of PBT on provision timing, which reverses as written-off loans become deductible; the expense rate is the better long-run measure.
base.terminal_note: Gordon growth governs (FCFE multiple (1+g)/(CoE-g) = 14.6x bear, 15.8x base, 17.3x bull); the 18x cap is set above all three so it does not bind. A 12-15x cap would have silently cut the base terminal value and removed the terminal-growth sensitivity the grid is meant to show.
base.narrative: NIM has bottomed: the 2024-25 LPR cuts are fully repriced on the deposit side, NIM holds 1.35-1.40%, loans grow ~7% along the Five Priorities, fee income compounds mid-single digits on a RMB23tn wealth franchise. Credit costs stay ~50bps as property and LGFV exposure is worked out slowly behind state-sponsored rollovers rather than recognised in a spike. Cost-to-income drifts to ~30%. CET1 held at 14.5% with the payout rising from 30% toward ~60% over a decade as RWA growth slows to nominal GDP. ROE on common ~9.5%, so the bank is worth about book.

bull.growth_rationale: NIM recovers to ~1.45-1.50% by FY2028 as deposit costs reset lower (deposit rate cuts of 2025 fully flow through) while the PBOC pauses, loans grow ~8% in a fiscal-stimulus upcycle, fee income grows double digits on wealth management, pension finance (Pillar 3) and investment banking (bond underwriting +86% FY2025). Terminal 3.5%.
bull.margin_rationale: Property stabilises in 2027, credit impairment falls to ~15-16% of operating income (~40bps), cost-to-income held ~28-29% on AI/digital efficiency ('AI+' initiative), AT1 distributions ~0.7%. ROE on common ~10.5-11%, back to the FY2024 level.
bull.capex_rationale: Retention on faster RWA growth (7.0%, 6.5%, 6.0%, 5.5%, 5.0%, 4.5%, 4.0%, then 3.5% = terminal) at 14.5% CET1 from the same RMB25.34tn opening base, as % of bull revenue; terminal retention = CET1 x g.
bull.narrative: The re-rating case: the PBOC easing cycle ends with NIM recovering to ~1.5%, a fiscal upcycle and a property floor let credit costs normalise to ~40bps, fee income compounds double digits as household savings rotate into wealth and pension products, and the Big Four lift payout ratios (the mooted ~31% interim step is the first move). ROE on common returns to ~10.5-11% and the H-share closes part of its 32% discount to the A-share.

bear.growth_rationale: Another two LPR cuts in 2027 push NIM to ~1.20-1.25% with deposits already near the floor; loan growth continues at policy pace (~7%) but at sub-economic pricing, so revenue is flat; fee income stalls with weak capital markets and bancassurance fee caps; the H1 2026 trading-gain surge reverses. Terminal 2.5%.
bear.margin_rationale: Credit cycle: property-developer, LGFV and mortgage losses that have been rolled over are recognised through FY2027-29, credit impairment rises to ~25-27% of operating income (~70-75bps of loans, roughly the FY2020 peak), cost-to-income rises to ~31-32% on flat revenue, AT1 distributions ~0.9%. ROE on common ~7-7.5% at the trough, recovering to ~8%.
bear.capex_rationale: Policy-directed balance-sheet growth does not slow when earnings do: RWA grow 7.0%, 6.5%, 5.5%, 4.5%, 3.5%, 3.0%, then 2.5% = terminal, at 14.5% CET1 from the same opening base, as % of bear revenue. Payout falls to ~18% of profit to common in FY2027-28 (in practice this is the path on which the MOF injects capital again and the ordinary dividend is held at the expense of dilution), recovering to ~60% at steady state.
bear.tax_rationale: Lower profit against the same non-taxable bond interest gives a lower effective rate in the trough years.
bear.narrative: The policy-bank case: the property downturn and LGFV restructuring finally hit the P&L as rollovers stop masking losses, impairment runs at ~70-75bps for three years while NIM compresses to ~1.2% on further easing; the state keeps the balance sheet growing at ~7% for policy reasons, so retained earnings cannot fund both the growth and the dividend, and the choice is dilution (another MOF placement) or a lower payout. ROE on common ~7%, and the H-share stays at 0.5-0.6x book as it did in 2022-24. RMB weakness against the HKD peg would compound this for H-share holders (not modelled in the CNY flows; carried by the bear weight).

scenario_narratives.base: NIM bottoms at ~1.35-1.40%, loans grow ~7% along the Five Priorities with revenue +4% fading to 3%, credit costs stay ~50bps behind state-sponsored rollovers, cost-to-income drifts to ~30%, CET1 held at 14.5% with the payout rising from 30% toward ~60% as RWA growth slows to nominal GDP. ROE on common ~9.5% against a 9.5% CoE: worth about book.
scenario_narratives.bull: PBOC easing ends with NIM recovering to ~1.5%, a fiscal upcycle floors property and credit costs normalise to ~40bps, fee income compounds double digits on wealth/pension finance, the Big Four lift payouts; ROE on common ~10.5-11% and the H-share narrows its 32% discount to the A-share.
scenario_narratives.bear: Property/LGFV losses are recognised through FY2027-29 at ~70-75bps while NIM compresses to ~1.2%; the state keeps RWA growing ~7% for policy reasons so earnings cannot fund both growth and the dividend (dilution or payout cut); ROE on common ~7%, stock stays at 0.5-0.6x book.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 30% and bull cut from 35% to 20%. Bear up: the bear axes are not tail events but the base case's own mechanisms running slightly further -- NIM has fallen every year since 2019 and has stabilised for exactly one half-year; real-estate development NPL is 4.93% with special-mention and restructured loans rising; credit is allocated by state mandate, not return; the 2025 MOF recapitalisation shows retained earnings already could not fund policy-pace growth at a 30% payout; and the market has priced 0.5-0.65x book for four years, i.e. it already assumes something like the bear path. Bull down: the bull case needs an independent NIM recovery, a property floor, double-digit fee growth and a state decision to raise payouts to happen together, and management's own 2026 commentary ('complex and challenging', 'safeguarding the bottom line of risks') is defensive. Base at 50%: the capital position (14.63% CET1, ~5.5pts above requirement), the sovereign backstop and the stabilising H1 2026 NIM make the central path the most likely.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A bank is worth the equity cash flow it can distribute after funding the capital its balance-sheet growth requires, discounted at the cost of equity in the flows' own currency. For CCB the question is less the earnings -- RMB340bn of profit on a 14.6% CET1 ratio is not in doubt -- than who the earnings belong to: a state owner that sets loan growth, loan pricing and the payout ratio, and that retains two-thirds of profit to fund policy lending at a ~10% ROE. The FCFE model counts capital retained above the 14.5% ratio as shareholder value once RWA growth slows; the market, at 0.63x book on the H-share, does not. At a 9.5% CNY cost of equity and a ~9.5% steady-state ROE the base value is ~0.87x book (RMB11.49 / HKD13.47 per share) -- below book because the first decade's payout is held at 30-40% by policy-pace RWA growth -- and the probability-weighted value (RMB11.23 / HKD13.17), with the bear at 30%, lands almost exactly at the Shanghai A-share price (RMB10.98), 35% above the H-share. The bear case itself (RMB8.90, 0.67x book) sits at the H-share price: the H-share is priced for a durable ~7-8% ROE. The gap to the H-share price is the discount for state control, RMB translation and latent property credit risk, not for the reported earnings. All flows, book and dividends are RMB; the HKD figure moves one-for-one with CNY/HKD.
key_risks_to_valuation: Credit cycle: every 10bps on the RMB27.8tn loan book is ~RMB28bn pre-tax, ~3.5pts of margin; real-estate development NPL 4.93%, mortgages ~22% of loans, LGFV rollovers masking losses.
NIM: each 5bps on ~RMB43tn of interest-earning assets is ~RMB21bn of revenue (~2.7% of operating income); the H1 2026 stabilisation at 1.37% is one half-year of evidence after four years of decline.
Policy-directed growth: if RWA keep growing ~7-8% while revenue is flat, retention consumes the whole surplus and the model's rising payout never materialises (the bear capex path).

Payout and capital policy set by the state: the 30% payout has been fixed since 2015; the 'excess' FCFE in later years is a modelling assumption about distributability that CCB has no buyback mechanism to deliver.
CNY/HKD: a 5% RMB depreciation against the HKD peg is a 5% cut to every HKD value in this file with no offset in the CNY model.
Cost of equity: the 9.5% CNY CoE is built on an assumed ~1.8% 10Y CGB; each 1pt on the CoE is roughly +/-17% on the base value (9.0% -> HKD14.71, 10.0% -> HKD12.41) (sensitivity grid).
Dilution: a second MOF-led recapitalisation (reported for ICBC/ABC, Sept 2026) is not modelled; at or above book it is roughly neutral, below book it is dilutive.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (regular HKEX close); 52-week range 7.18-9.90. Parity vs Shanghai 601939.SS and CNYHKD=X in inputs.fx_note.
data_sources.financials: 0939.HK_Metrics.csv (FY2018-FY2025 from the H-share annual reports; operating income, attributable profit, equity incl. AT1 instruments, EPS, plus kpis NIM/ROE/CET1/RWA/NPL/impairment); 0939.HK_Annual_FY2025.txt (five-year financial summary lines 720-760, income statement 9850-9880, equity 10037-10047, share-capital table 8215-8262, other-equity-instrument distributions 15258-15282, income-tax note 12207-12214, quarterly operating income line 811); H1 2026 headline figures from Analysis.json (interim not extracted).
data_sources.qualitative: 0939.HK_Analysis.json (2026-10-12): FY2025 and H1 2026 results, NIM/NPL/capital trends, Five Priorities lending, 30% payout policy, MOF recapitalisation, property/LGFV and policy-lending risks, bull/bear axes.

sanity_check_note.status: expected tool artefact on a dual-currency ticker, not a real trip
sanity_check_note.detail: scripts/sanity_check.py applies inputs.fx_rate (CNY->HKD, 1.1721) in the opposite direction to dcf_engine.py (known systemic fx-direction bug in memory), so its printed multiples will be off by a factor of ~1.37 (1.1721^2) on the historical side. Hand-computed multiples below are the check.

hand_computed_multiples.basis: HKD price / 1.1721 = RMB per share; profit to common = attributable profit less AT1/preference distributions; common book = equity attributable less other equity instruments (RMB13.24/share at 2025-12-31)
hand_computed_multiples.history_10yr_approx: The H-share has traded ~0.4-0.9x book and ~4-7x earnings over 2016-2025 (0.5-0.6x in 2022-24, ~0.65x after the 2025-26 rerating); the A-share ~0.6-1.0x. Chinese megabanks have not traded above book since 2018, so a base value near 1.0x book is the arithmetic of ROE ~ CoE, not a multiple the market has recently paid -- which is why the bear carries 30%.
